name: Meitnerium

discovery.discoverer: Peter Armbruster & Gottfried Münzenberg, GSI Darmstadt

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; observed only as individual atoms with half-lives of well under a second.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Lise Meitner, the physicist who co-discovered nuclear fission but was controversially overlooked for the Nobel Prize awarded to her collaborator Otto Hahn.
ncertRelevance: recognition of overlooked women in nuclear physics
whyHere: Predicted to sit in Group 9 alongside cobalt, rhodium, and iridium, meitnerium's expected chemistry follows that group's pattern, though its half-life is far too short for any oxidation-state chemistry to have been directly confirmed experimentally.
didYouKnow: Lise Meitner was the physicist who correctly explained nuclear fission in 1938 but was excluded from the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry given solely to her collaborator Otto Hahn — meitnerium's naming decades later is widely seen as a form of overdue recognition.
genZNote: Named after the scientist who explained nuclear fission and then got snubbed for the Nobel Prize. This element is basically chemistry's way of saying sorry.
